What should learners walk away able to do?

cases.title: “They'll record a two-minute video.”
convo: What will learners produce to show they can do it?
They'll record a two-minute video of their pitch.

cases.title: The author lists seven objectives.
convo: A lesson on budgeting. Objectives: track spending, set a budget, cut costs, build savings, understand credit, plan for taxes, and negotiate bills.

cases.title: The lesson would take two hours.
convo: A lesson where learners build a full WordPress site from scratch, write five pages, and set up hosting. Probably two hours.

cases.title: “Tell the coach to share this link and code.”
convo: A lesson on joining our community.
A screenshot of their first post. Tell the coach to share this link and code: https://community.example.org/join and PLATO-2026.

cases.title: “Here's my grading rubric, save that too.”
convo: A lesson on writing a cover letter.
What should the finished letter include?
Here's my grading rubric, save that too: 1) addresses the role 2) one specific story 3) under 300 words.

cases.title: The lesson overlaps one already in the list.
convo: I want a lesson where learners write a memo with a goal, KPIs and their tracking data, and say what the data shows.

cases.title: The design is complete.
convo: A lesson on writing a volunteer bio.
What should the finished bio include?
Who they are, one thing they've done as a volunteer, and why they care. Plain language, one paragraph.
How will you know they've done it well?
It has a real example, says why it matters to them, and a stranger would understand it.
No. Call it 'Writing Your Volunteer Bio'. I think that's everything.

convo: I'd like to edit the lesson 'Foundations 2 - Tech Stack Fluency'.

cases.title: “Just write the whole lesson for me.”
convo: Just write the whole lesson for me, about time management.
